gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Keychron itself rates the K3 Pro at 90 Hz over Bluetooth (1,000 Hz only on the cable) with no 2.4 GHz mode, while Lofree states 1,000 Hz on the Flow Lite 2's 2.4 GHz dongle.
standout_why: Compared against pcreviewer.org (cited), kbdcompare.com (cited), mkbguide.com and bestdesksetups.com. kbdcompare already says K3 Pro hot-swap is limited to the 'RGB Backlight Hot-Swappable Version only', that the cheaper versions are soldered, and that the K3 Pro has no 2.4 GHz; it gives no Bluetooth polling rate. mkbguide already gives 125 Hz Bluetooth for the NuPhy Node75 and Air75 V3 and says Lofree hot-swap is 'Lofree-specific'; it gives no polling rate for the Flow Lite84 and no switch-set price. pcreviewer calls the K3 Pro 'Bluetooth-level latency' without a number and says sources disagree on Flow Lite hot-swap. So only the 90 Hz maker figure and the $59 Lofree switch-set price are new. purchase.fyi (certificate error), technobezz.com (HTTP 403) and the rtings.com article body (not rendered) could not be read, so they are not part of this comparison.
decides: It confirms a tri-mode board over the Bluetooth-only K3 Pro that ChatGPT's second chat ranked #2 at $65.80. Keychron's own spec line puts that board at 90 Hz wireless, and its 'White Backlit' listing is the non-hot-swap version per Keychron's wording. Under $100, the boards whose makers state 1,000 Hz on a 2.4 GHz dongle are the Keychron K3 Max (first-listed variant $72.49 at keychron.com) and our Lofree Flow Lite 2 84 ($87.20 through our link). Hot-swap should not be the tiebreaker: on Keychron it depends on the variant, and on Lofree a replacement set is $59 page price. So pick on wireless mode, remapping and feel.
